champion: Amyloid light-chain amyloidosis with multiple myeloma
ordered_diagnoses: Amyloid light-chain amyloidosis with multiple myeloma

facts.raw_span: 1-week history of progressive, painful blisters and ulcers of the groin
enlargement of the tongue over the past 3 months, leading to difficulty with mastication
numbness without weakness of her distal lower limbs for 3 months
IgG λ-type multiple myeloma complicated by anemia and lytic lesions in the calvarium
Circinate purpuric patches with erosions on the natal cleft, buttocks, inguinal creases, and vulva
Hemorrhagic flaccid bullae on the posterior perineum
Macroglossia, glossitis, and a hemorrhagic erosion on the hard palate
Purpuric macules present periorbitally, on the lips, inframammary folds, forearms, and thighs
Platelet count: 171 × 10^3/μL
Serum zinc: 34.4 μg/dL

subepidermal blister lined by fibrin and chronic inflammatory infiltrate, with scattered short eosinophilic bands in the dermis showing apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy with Congo red staining
Herpes simplex virus PCR from perineal ulcer swab was negative

Serum zinc: 34.4 μg/dL

subepidermal blister lined by fibrin and chronic inflammatory infiltrate, with scattered short eosinophilic bands in the dermis showing apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy with Congo red staining
Herpes simplex virus PCR from perineal ulcer swab was negative

concepts.why: The patient's IgG λ-type multiple myeloma, macroglossia, and subepidermal blister with apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy are consistent with primary systemic amyloidosis.
The patient's low serum zinc level and symptoms of glossitis and macroglossia are consistent with acquired zinc deficiency.
The patient's purpuric patches, hemorrhagic bullae, and inflammatory infiltrate are consistent with leukocytoclastic vasculitis.
The patient's IgG λ-type multiple myeloma is a known diagnosis.
The patient's symptoms of glossitis, macroglossia, and purpuric macules are consistent with Sjögren's syndrome.
The patient's numbness without weakness and use of intramuscular cyanocobalamin supplements are consistent with vitamin B12 deficiency.
The patient's anemia and use of folic acid and intramuscular cyanocobalamin supplements are consistent with pernicious anemia.

concepts.preferred_label: Amyloid light-chain amyloidosis with multiple myeloma
concepts.why: The patient's IgG λ-type multiple myeloma, macroglossia, and subepidermal blister with apple-green birefringence on polarized light microscopy are consistent with amyloid light-chain amyloidosis with multiple myeloma.
The negative Herpes simplex virus PCR from perineal ulcer swab, in combination with the patient's skin findings, points towards a diagnosis of Amyloidosis cutis dyschromica.
